value.title: Engine-selection seam, pipeline.engine config, and eligibility probe
value.description: Introduce the engine-selection seam at the frozen runPipeline boundary. Add pipeline.engine to the Zod config (enum ts|skill|workflow, default 'ts'). Extract the current runPipeline body into a TS engine that implements a new PipelineEngine interface, and make the exported runPipeline a thin seam that resolves config.pipeline.engine via a PipelineEngineSelector and dispatches. Add a WorkflowEligibilityCheck probe that reports ineligible by default; selecting 'workflow' when ineligible (or mode='careful') resolves the TS engine and logs exactly one downgrade line. No behavior change on the default path.

successCriteria.description: pipeline.engine exists in PipelineSectionSchema as z.enum(['ts','skill','workflow']) defaulting to 'ts', mirrored in createDefaultConfig; a schema unit test asserts the default and rejects an unknown engine string.

A PipelineEngine interface { name; run(userPrompt, projectRoot, config): Promise<PipelineResult> } and PipelineEngineName type exist; a TsPipelineEngine wraps the extracted runPipeline body and a PipelineEngineSelector with pure resolveEngineName + select resolves config.pipeline.engine.

resolveEngineName returns 'ts' when engine is unset; returns 'ts' (downgrade) when engine='workflow' and the eligibility probe is ineligible OR mode='careful'; returns 'skill'/'workflow' verbatim only when eligible. A unit test covers each branch and asserts exactly one downgrade log line on the workflow→ts case.

The exported async runPipeline(userPrompt, projectRoot, config): Promise<PipelineResult> signature is unchanged and now delegates to selector.select(config).run(...); the TS engine path is the unchanged former body.
npm run typecheck and npm run build exit 0, and the existing orchestrator/pipeline test suite stays green with no new failures beyond the documented flaky tool-count baseline.

Do not make the eligibility probe actually contact the runtime; a conservative default-ineligible probe is sufficient this sprint.
Do not touch agents/*.md, the contracts protocol, or providers/types.ts.

value.title: EvaluatorPanelReconciler — pure TS majority-vote reducer
value.description: Implement reconcile(sprintId, round, lensVerdicts): EvalResult as a pure, side-effect-free majority-vote reducer over per-lens EvalResult[] (ADR-4). It produces a canonical EvalResult with evaluator='panel', passed=strict-majority, fail-closed on tie, unioning failing details and feedback from minority/failing lenses. The timestamp is supplied by the caller (no Date.now). Empty input throws. This is the conformance-critical core; the JS port and drift gate follow in sprint 3.

successCriteria.description: reconcile is a pure function with signature reconcile(sprintId: string, round: number, lensVerdicts: EvalResult[], timestamp: string): EvalResult; it calls no Date.now/Math.random and performs no fs/IO, verified by code inspection and a passing unit suite.

passed=true only when a strict majority of lenses have passed=true; a tie (equal pass/fail) yields passed=false (fail-closed), asserted by unit tests for unanimous-pass, unanimous-fail, majority-pass, majority-fail, and 2v2 tie vectors.

The canonical result has evaluator='panel', details = the union of all failing details across lenses (de-duplicated by criterion+message), and feedback aggregating the failing lenses' feedback; the injected timestamp is used verbatim.
reconcile([]) throws a descriptive error; a single-lens input returns that lens's verdict re-stamped as evaluator='panel'.
The returned object validates against EvalResultSchema (zod safeParse success), and npm run typecheck + npm run build exit 0 with the new suite green.

nonGoals: Do not write the pure-JS port or any .claude/workflows/ file — that is sprint 3.
Do not wire reconcile into any pipeline or script yet.
Do not introduce a new EvalResult shape; reuse the frozen EvalResultSchema from src/contracts/eval-result.ts.
Do not generate the timestamp inside the reducer.

value.definitionOfDone: A pure reconcile reducer producing a canonical evaluator='panel' EvalResult by strict-majority vote (fail-closed on tie) with unioned failing details and a caller-injected timestamp; empty input throws; output validates against EvalResultSchema; comprehensive unit tests over ties/mixed/empty-detail/unanimous vectors pass; typecheck and build green.
assumptions: Strict majority means passCount > failCount; equal counts fail closed.
Detail de-duplication by (criterion, message) is acceptable for the union; severity is preserved from the first occurrence.
value.generatorNotes: Create src/orchestrator/workflow/reconciler.ts. Import type { EvalResult, EvalDetail } from '../../contracts/eval-result.js'. Signature: `export function reconcile(sprintId: string, round: number, lensVerdicts: EvalResult[], timestamp: string): EvalResult`. Algorithm: throw if lensVerdicts.length===0. passCount = lenses with passed===true. passed = passCount > (lensVerdicts.length - passCount). Build details: concat all details where passed===false across lenses, de-dup by `${criterion}␟${message}`. summary: e.g. `Panel verdict: ${passCount}/${n} lenses passed`. feedback: join failing lenses' feedback with newlines (or 'All lenses passed.' when passed). Set evaluator:'panel', timestamp (the injected arg), passed, details, summary, feedback. Optionally compute score as round(100*passCount/n). Keep it pure — no Date, no Math.random, no IO. Single-lens: return that lens re-stamped (evaluator:'panel', timestamp). Add a unicode section header. Create src/orchestrator/workflow/reconciler.test.ts with Vitest: cases for n=1, unanimous pass, unanimous fail, 3-pass/2-fail (majority pass), 2-pass/3-fail (majority fail), 2v2 tie (fail-closed), empty (expect throw), empty-detail lenses, and a zod safeParse assertion on the output. ESM .js specifiers, import type for types. Conventional commit: bober(sprint-2): add pure EvaluatorPanelReconciler majority-vote reducer.
value.evaluatorNotes: Inspect reconciler.ts for any Date.now/new Date()/Math.random/fs usage — there must be none. Run npx vitest run src/orchestrator/workflow/reconciler.test.ts and confirm all vectors pass, especially the 2v2 tie → passed:false and empty → throw. Confirm the output object passes EvalResultSchema.safeParse (the test should assert this; if not, run a quick check). value.title: Workflow types, ResumeCursorReconstructor, and ArgsPayloadBuilder
value.description: Add the new TS types (WorkflowArgs, WorkflowRunResult, ResumeCursor, ConformanceReport) and the host-side input plumbing. ResumeCursorReconstructor re-derives completed-sprint state from durable contract status + history for crash-safe resume. ArgsPayloadBuilder marshals config, principles, models, and lenses into one JSON-serializable WorkflowArgs, throwing MissingKnobError on an unset required knob, AgentCapError when the worst-case agent count (maxSprints × maxIterations × lenses) exceeds the 16/1000 caps, and NonSerializableArgError on a non-serializable model.

successCriteria.description: src/orchestrator/workflow/types.ts defines WorkflowArgs, WorkflowRunResult, ResumeCursor, and ConformanceReport exactly per the architecture data model, reusing frozen PlanSpec/SprintContract/EvalResult/HistoryEntry types from src/contracts/.

ResumeCursorReconstructor.reconstruct(projectRoot, specId) returns a ResumeCursor whose completedSprintNumbers are derived from durable contract status (status passed/completed) via loadHistory + contract reads; with no history it returns completedSprintNumbers:[]; when contract status disagrees with history it trusts contract status. Unit tests cover all three.

ArgsPayloadBuilder.build(userPrompt, config, cursor) returns a fully JSON-serializable WorkflowArgs (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(args)) deep-equals args), with knobs/models/evaluatorLenses populated from config (lenses from config.evaluator.strategies or a sensible default).

build throws MissingKnobError when a required knob is unset, AgentCapError when maxSprints × maxIterations × lenses > 16 concurrent or > 1000 total (computed worst-case, pre-invoke), and NonSerializableArgError on a non-serializable model value; each path has a unit test.
npm run typecheck and npm run build exit 0 and the new suites are green.

nonGoals: Do not write bober-pipeline.js or the RunResultFlusher (sprint 5) or the WorkflowEngine (sprint 6).
Do not perform any agent dispatch.
Do not change the contracts protocol or history schema; only read them.
Do not introduce SDK types into these modules.

value.title: bober-pipeline.js workflow script and RunResultFlusher
value.description: Author the pure-JS workflow script .claude/workflows/bober-pipeline.js that orchestrates plan→curate→generate→adversarial-panel→reconcile→retry via agent({agentType}) in parity with the TS pipeline stages, owning no truth, skipping resumeCursor.completedSprintNumbers, chunking the panel ≤16, and returning a WorkflowRunResult. Implement the host-side RunResultFlusher.flush that commits a WorkflowRunResult to durable .bober/ state (saveContract/updateContract, appendHistory, updateProgress), stamping ISO timestamps as the only clock source, atomic per file, flushing after each contract for crash-safety. Since live invoke is dormant, the script is authored + parse/lint-checked and the flusher is unit-tested with a synthetic WorkflowRunResult.

successCriteria.description: .claude/workflows/bober-pipeline.js begins with a literal `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` block (pure literal) and exposes a main(args) flow that calls agent({agentType,...}) for planner/curator/generator/evaluator and uses the JS reconcile port from ./lib/reconcile.js; it parses as an ES module (node --check or an import in a test).

The script logic skips contracts whose sprintNumber is in resumeCursor.completedSprintNumbers, runs the evaluator panel per lens with chunking so no fan-out exceeds 16, branches the retry loop on reconcile().passed, and returns a WorkflowRunResult shape (verified by extracting/importing its pure helper functions in a unit test, or by a structural assertion on a dry-run harness).

RunResultFlusher.flush(projectRoot, config, result) persists the spec, each contract (saveContract/updateContract), appends history (appendHistory) and updates progress (updateProgress), stamping ISO timestamps on pendingHistory entries and contract completedAt; it returns a PipelineResult. A unit test with a synthetic WorkflowRunResult asserts the written .bober/ files.

flush is crash-safe: it commits after each contract (not once at end) and is idempotent — re-flushing the same result does not duplicate history beyond the documented commit-by-message idempotency; a unit test re-runs flush and asserts no duplicate contract corruption.
npm run typecheck, npm run build, and the lint command exit 0; the new flusher and script suites are green within npm run test.

nonGoals: Do not execute the script against the live Workflows runtime — it is dormant this release.
Do not implement WorkflowEngine.run/invoke or the eligibility wiring (sprint 6).
Do not implement careful-flow stage-splitting.
Do not let the script perform fs, Date.now, or Math.random — all clock/fs work is host-side in the flusher.

Stop when changes are confined to .claude/workflows/bober-pipeline.js, src/orchestrator/workflow/flusher.ts, and their tests.

Start with `export const meta = { name: 'bober-pipeline', description: '...', phases: [{title:'Plan'},{title:'Sprint'}] }` (PURE literal — no variables). value.title: WorkflowEngine assembly, selector integration, and EngineConformanceHarness
value.description: Assemble WorkflowEngine (implements PipelineEngine name='workflow') wiring ResumeCursorReconstructor → ArgsPayloadBuilder → invoke → RunResultFlusher. invoke probes eligibility and, when ineligible (the dormant default) or on WorkflowUnavailableError from the first invoke, re-dispatches the TS engine before any .bober/ flush. Register the workflow engine in the selector so engine='workflow' resolves it (then downgrades). Implement EngineConformanceHarness.assertEquivalent asserting ts vs skill emit equivalent .bober/ artifacts for a fixture spec, and wire it as a CI gate. This closes the loop: engine='workflow' completes via TS downgrade in CI with no partial flush.

successCriteria.description: WorkflowEngine implements PipelineEngine with name='workflow' and a run() that builds a cursor + args, calls invoke, and flushes; on WorkflowUnavailableError from the first invoke it re-dispatches the TS engine and no .bober/ contract/eval artifact is written by the workflow path before the re-dispatch. A unit test forces the unavailable path and asserts TS re-dispatch with zero partial flush.

The selector registers and resolves the workflow engine: with engine='workflow' and the dormant ineligible probe, select() returns a path that completes via TS downgrade with exactly one downgrade log line; engine='ts' and 'skill' resolve unchanged. Unit tests cover each.
